note: doc 06 section 2.6, the named combinations for each unit. Every row states what the pairing or trio gives AND what it costs: a library that lists only benefits is marketing, not coaching, so what_it_costs is required and the seed validator rejects an empty one. Some of these named combinations deliberately trip a unit_balance_rules row (the gegenpress trio has no tempo setter, the rotating trio has two). That is not a contradiction: the rules are checks, the cost line says the same thing in words, and doc 06 names both as good combinations anyway.

items.name: Control, Unlock, Finish
items.what_it_gives: The positional-possession trio. One player controls the tempo, one unlocks the last line, one arrives from deep to finish the move.
items.what_it_costs: The crasher's flank is exposed on the turnover, because he is inside their box at the moment the ball changes hands.
items.reference_note: The trio positional-possession sides keep returning to. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: The Gegenpress Trio
items.what_it_gives: Wins the ball high and drives at a defence that has not had time to set itself.
items.what_it_costs: Limited against a low block, because carrying into a packed box is not a plan. Nobody in the trio sets a tempo, so it struggles to control a game it is already leading.
items.reference_note: Liverpool in the 2018 to 2020 window. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Double Pivot By Rotation
items.what_it_gives: Builds as a two and attacks as a two, changing shape by rotation rather than by substitution.
items.what_it_costs: It demands very high tactical discipline about who drops. Two of the three can set tempo, so they have to agree who accelerates once the line is broken.

items.name: The Tournament Trio
items.what_it_gives: Balanced across all three midfield duties: tempo, rest defence, and progression, with no obvious hole to attack.
items.what_it_costs: Nobody drives with the ball, so the last twenty metres depend entirely on the front three.

items.name: Screen and Circulate
items.what_it_gives: One holds the ball, one holds the space. The pair is hard to play through and always offers a safe pass backwards.
items.what_it_costs: Neither of them breaks a line, so the ten and the wide forwards have to create everything on their own.
items.reference_note: The default 4-2-3-1 pairing. Bible 4.2 names the failure case, two destroyers together, as the sterile pivot.

items.name: Playmaker and Runner
items.what_it_gives: One picks the vertical pass, one runs past the ball into the box, so the pivot both builds the attack and arrives in it.
items.what_it_costs: Neither of them is a screen. Once the shuttler goes and the line breaker steps up with the ball, the counter comes straight back through the middle.

items.name: Carry and Screen
items.what_it_gives: Beats the first press by carrying rather than passing, with a screen sitting behind the carry the whole time.
items.what_it_costs: There is no tempo setter in the pair, so possession is either forward or lost. Against a set block it will look rushed.

items.name: Width, Depth, and a Cut Inside
items.what_it_gives: One holds the width, one holds the depth, one arrives in the box from the far half-space. The back four is stretched in both directions.
items.what_it_costs: Only one of the three tracks back, so the fullback behind the inside forward is left alone on every turnover.

items.name: The False Nine Front Three
items.what_it_gives: The nine drops to make a midfield overload and the wide forwards attack the space he leaves on the last line.
items.what_it_costs: If the centre backs refuse to follow the nine, the team has a spare man in midfield and nobody in the box.
items.reference_note: Barcelona under Guardiola. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: The Pressing Front Three
items.what_it_gives: Sets the trap from the front, wins the ball inside forty metres of their goal, and finishes through the inside forward.
items.what_it_costs: It is a fitness bet. Once the front three cannot repeat the sprints, the block sits ten metres deeper and the same players look passive.

items.name: Runner and Target
items.what_it_gives: One occupies the centre backs in the air and one occupies the space behind them, so the defence has no single reference point.
items.what_it_costs: Neither of them drops into midfield, so a two-versus-three in the middle third is the standing price of the pair.

items.name: Two Runners
items.what_it_gives: Both attack the space behind, which pushes a high line back thirty metres from the very first pass.
items.what_it_costs: It needs a ten who can find them or an identity that plays long. Without one of those, the pair is isolated and the midfield is outnumbered.

items.name: False and Poacher
items.what_it_gives: One drops off to build the chance, one stays on the last shoulder to finish it, and the centre backs have to split their attention.
items.what_it_costs: The poacher touches the ball a handful of times a game. If the chances do not arrive, the team is playing with ten.

items.name: Stopper and Coverer
items.what_it_gives: One meets the ball in front of the line and one defends the space behind it, which is the minimum a back four needs.
items.what_it_costs: Neither is picked to build, so the first pass out has to come from the fullbacks or the goalkeeper.

items.name: Builder and Stopper
items.what_it_gives: One breaks the first line with a pass and one defends on the front foot, which suits a side that presses high and plays out.
items.what_it_costs: Neither is picked for pure recovery pace, so depth is defended by the goalkeeper or by a very disciplined offside line.

items.name: Stepping Back Three
items.what_it_gives: One side of the three carries the ball out, the other follows his man, and the middle sweeps behind both of them.
items.what_it_costs: It only holds up if the wingbacks drop into a five. If they stay high, the three is defending the full width of the pitch alone.

items.name: Overlap Pair
items.what_it_gives: The winger comes inside and takes his marker with him, the fullback runs into the space outside and delivers from the byline.
items.what_it_costs: Both end up ahead of the ball, so the flank is a corridor on the turnover. This is the double exposure the roster already warns about.

items.name: Inverted Fullback and Touchline Winger
items.what_it_gives: The fullback steps in to overload the middle and protect the counter, the winger holds the chalk and keeps their fullback pinned.
items.what_it_costs: The winger is alone in his one-versus-one all game. If he does not beat his man, that flank produces nothing at all.

items.name: Wingback and Inside Forward
items.what_it_gives: The wingback supplies the width and the depth on his own, and the wide forward plays inside him in the half-space.
items.what_it_costs: One player covers the whole flank in both directions, which is a bet on his fitness and on his recovery pace.
